newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 8.

text.p: Computer Associates International Inc agreed to buy Cheyenne Software Inc for $1.2 billion in cash. Cheyenne's share price jumped 34 percent on the news, the Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday.
* Texaco Inc, Royal Dutch/Shell Group and Saudi Aramco confirmed they were talking about merging their downstream operations.
* Sony Corp is to announce a new Sony Pictures management team, including a Japanese executive who is to act as a liaison with Tokyo.
* TCW Group Inc, parent of Trust Co of the West, said it was reviewing strategic alternatives including selling the firm, which manages more than $50 billion in pension money and mutual funds.
* Drug company Quintiles Transnational Corp agreed to buy British contract pharmaceutical maker Innovex Inc for $787.8 million in stock, plus debt assumption.
* HFS Inc agreed to purchase Resort Condominiums International for $625 million in cash and stock.
* Motorola Inc's quarterly profit fell 58 percent and the company said its problems would likely persist.
* General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union continue labor contract negotiations as 6,000 unionized workers prepare to join more than 20,000 striking others on Wednesday.
* U.S. Supreme Court turned down Unisys Corp's request to reject complaints made by employees that it made bad investments in two retirement funds.
* Fidelity's Magellan fund hastened its shift from bonds to stocks as the mutual fund suffers from withdrawals of investor cash.
* The White House withdrew its support for a new digital television standard in response to complaints from Microsoft Corp and Hollywood.
* Ousted chief executive officer Steven Scott apparently won a proxy vote for control of Coastal Physician Group Inc.
* Anti-trust enforcers are scrutinizing many of the radio station purchases announced in the wake of this year's telecommunications law.
* Dow Jones industrials fell 13.05 points to 5,979.81 after surpassing the 6,000-point mark, while the NASDAQ Composite Index and S&P 500 set records at the end of trading.

* Takeover gossip is pushing some stock prices higher in advance of a regulatory move that the U.S. Federal Reserve could make next month to expand the amount of corporate debt and equity underwriting that banks can do. An increase could allow commercial banks to buy securities.
* The bond market retreated amid profit taking and supply pressure following Friday's steep run up on a weak September employment report.
